in.role: Giants TE1 and the No. 2 target behind Malik Nabers; top-five Week 1 TE on SI's board

out.role: Arizona's listed RB1 only while Jeremiyah Love is hurt, in an 18.75-point implied total
out.alert: Arizona are 10-point dogs with the lowest implied total on the slate

doFirst.why: Likely is rostered in 82.5% of ESPN leagues and is sitting here as a free agent, costing nothing. He moved to New York this offseason and is the clear No. 2 target behind Nabers, who is a game-time decision and being eased back in - SI have Likely top five at the position this week. Allgeier is the opposite trade: ESPN's 7.6 and the Cardinals' official depth chart both say RB1, but Love was limited all three practices rather than building up, is expected to play on a pitch count, and Arizona are 10-point underdogs with an 18.75 implied total against a Chargers defense that allowed a league-low 9.7 passing points per game and ranked fourth in the red zone. Allgeier's job disappears the week Love is healthy; Likely's does not.

action.label: Add Isaiah Likely, drop Tyler Allgeier

trades.headline: They start a 16-point quarterback and you have a 17.6 sitting on your bench doing nothing
trades.yourSurplus: Josh Allen is your quarterback every week. Stafford is a bye-week seat that scores you zero points until Week 7, and he has already played this week for 4.1.
trades.theirHole: Los Gigantes start the lowest-projected quarterback in the league at 16 and carry no backup. Stafford is an immediate +0.9 to their starting lineup.
trades.yourLineup: Odunze slots into the RB/WR flex ahead of nobody this week, so the one-week gain is only +0.2. The point is shape, not this Sunday: you convert a dead roster seat into a startable third receiver behind Jefferson and Garrett Wilson.
trades.theirLineup: Stafford replaces their starter outright and gives them a real bye-week plan.
trades.risk: Priced on one week, which is the wrong unit and undersells your side. Only weekly projections are published, so a +0.2 headline is what the model can see; the roster-shape argument is judgement. If you think Stafford is your insurance against a Josh Allen injury, do not make this trade.

candidates.note: Tre Tucker, Raiders, free agent. Bowers had a meniscus procedure and is out, and Tucker played 94.9% of the Raiders' offensive snaps last season - the highest share among their receivers - so he absorbs part of the vacated target load against a Miami defence DraftKings Network called a favourable matchup. The counterweight, from that same piece: he is not the clear No. 1, Kubiak will spread the work, and 60% of his touchdowns last season came in a single game against Washington. A flex-quality dart, not a starter. Kicks off 20:25Z.

Michael Mayer, Raiders, free agent, and the biggest ownership riser on this wire at +3.91 - that move is entirely Bowers' knee. He is the Raiders' starting tight end while Bowers is out. Two sources split: SI say you must pick him up, Pro Football Network rank him TE37 and say sit, because nobody is confident where the Vegas targets go. Believe PFN for this week and SI for the stash - Bowers is expected back in a game or two, which caps the window either way. You already own him in IPADE; that does not make him right here, where Kyle Pitts is your tight end.

Mark Andrews, Ravens, on waivers until 2026-09-16T07:00Z, 83.4% rostered. Chem resets waiver priority every week, so a claim here costs you nothing lasting - this is the one league where a speculative claim is genuinely free. Worth a claim only if Kyle Pitts' zero today turns into a pattern; you cannot drop anyone else to make room until Monday anyway.

Xavier Worthy, Chiefs, free agent at 75.4% rostership - the kind of number that usually means someone blundered. It is not a blunder here. He is still working back from shoulder surgery and Sharp Football grade him a WR4/flex this week against a Denver defence that gave up 9.0 fantasy points per game to opposing WR1s and finished second in completion rate, yards per attempt and touchdown rate. Leave him. Monday night, 2026-09-15T00:15Z.
